name: A partner's own chips on one field
result: On the party's core with two MegaMen against BlastMan (layer 3 of --seed 3, --dev partycore=2,partytwin=1,partyroll=30,partybot=1): the two-a-side's answering hooks at BN6_NAVI_STATS_ADDR and BN6_HAND_ADDR, its marks at BN6_SPAWN_COMMON and BN6_SPAWN_MADE and its hold at BN6_LINK_SEND and BN6_CUSTOM_WAIT_LOOP, taken on a single-player battle's core with the partner read from side 0's slot 1; his record compiled by BN6 from his NaviCust over the party's kept boot (HP 100, Custom 5) in the fourth kind's last three slots, his deck dealt in RAM_TEAM_ROOMS as the field's first Custom screen opened (30 chips). His own BN6 Custom screen, a core of its own copied from the field with his deck at BN6_BATTLE_DECK, his record at BN6_BATTLE_NAVI and BN6_BATTLE_STEP put back to 0, dealt his hand and ran its rules: his OK's three picks (0C0, 09A, 036) crossed in his stream, his own hand took them at iteration 1 while the lead's held its own, and his A used his first chip at iteration 4831 (his hand's chip up next 0 to 1, the lead's at 2). A second core from the same keys agreed at every 60th frame and a 30-frame rollback every 30 ran again to the same hash, 308 checks and none apart, to the battle's end at frame 6176 (lost); the same build run twice gave the same ready hash (f41d5584e539094b) and end.
meaning: The two-a-side's per-object NaviStats and hands answer for three partners on one side of a single-player battle as they do for one a side of a link battle, and BN6's Custom screen runs a partner's own turn on a lone core copied from a single-player battle (no cable to miss, unlike the pair's). Not yet seen: the lead's OK held past it while a partner still picks (the single-player screen's mode 0x14 sends its packet through BN6_LINK_SEND as a link battle's does, bn6f sub_8026DC4, so the two-a-side's hold is built there), two or three games over the server, a partner's Program Advance, Cross and Souls.
